thread:
maria: Folks, seeing a customer report where a retry + cross-region routing caused two quota charges despite an idempotency key being present. anyone seen this pattern?

devon: Yup. a few things to check: are they canonicalizing the idempotency key per-org? we had a case where same key got rewritten by a proxy.

aisha: Also check whether the retry hit a fallback model variant in another region — we only dedupe within the same serving shard today.

raj: can you paste any logs or request headers? that helps rule out client-side bug.

maria: here's the raw header we captured from the customer's proxy:```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Idempotency-Key: 3f9b2f8a-...
x-org-id: org_8675309
User-Agent: my-app/2.1.0
```

maria: they send the same Idempotency-Key on retry. trace shows the first request reserved quota in region-us, second retry routed to region-eu because us pool was at burst cap. both ended up consuming quota.

devon: aha. so two independent reserve operations succeeded because dedupe is scoped to (shard + idempotency_key). cross-region routing breaks that.

kat: we have two design choices: 1) make idempotency canonicalization global (put canonical key into central index) so reservations are atomically visible across regions, or 2) bind reservations to a stronger reservation token thats checked at execution time. both have pros/cons for latency.

santana: Option 1 requires a cross-region lock/lookup on every request — big perf hit. Option 2 sounds interesting: client sends Idempotency-Key, we issue a short-lived reservation token from central ledger, then routing only consumes quota if token is still valid.

raj: can we do a hybrid fast-path? if org traffic is within single-region SLA, use local dedupe. if a retry is routed elsewhere, fallback to checking central ledger asynchronously with a small window (100ms) to prevent double-reserve on hot paths.

aisha: for UX we should expose in console a metric: `pending_reservations` and `reservation_conflicts`. make it visible per-org and per-key-rate. currently ops only sees final consumption, not the transient reserves.

maria: agreed — customer was confused because console showed 2x usage spikes but their app only retried once. having a "pending reservations" line item would help troubleshooting + billing disputes.

devon: implementation note: we also need to canonicalize incoming idempotency keys by prepending org id and normalizing whitespace/case so proxies can't mutate. e.g. canonical_key = sha256(org_id + '|' + trim(lower(idempotency_key))).

kat: +1. also add a server-side audit log entry when we convert a key, something like `idemp_canonicalized=true` so support can trace why two keys didn't dedupe.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout plan suggested: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with feature-flag `global_reserve_check`. monitor `reservation_conflicts` and `p99_latency_reserve`.

santana: question on billing: do we charge at reserve time or at execution time? current model charges on execution, but customers see spikes because reserve->fail->retry flow still leads to ledger entries. we might need a refundable reservation bucket in ledger to avoid double-charge during retries.

maria: i'd prefer reserving a non-billable hold then convert to billable on successful completion. that would prevent double-charge but adds complexity to accounting. finance? (cc @kat for design implications)

kat: looks doable but we need clear visibility in invoices: shows holds and final charges. also need guardrails so holds don't pile up (expire after X minutes).

raj: next steps proposal: 1) short-term: canonicalize idempotency keys (org prefix + normalize) + console metric for pending_reservations 2) medium-term: implement central reservation token with fast-path local cache fallback 3) billing: implement refundable hold flow with TTL.

maria: thanks — i'll open a GH issue with the proposal and link it to the canary flag. i'll also ask support to surface any active billing disputes related to this pattern.

devon: one last thing: update SDKs to recommend sending a stable `Idempotency-Key` + `x-org-id` header together; add a snippet in docs. small client changes reduce surface area.

maria: ok i'll draft the docs snippet. thanks all :thumbsup:
